Subject: ZenithShore RFP - follow up: implementation/canary details

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has requested a more detailed technical validation for our integration and a canary inventory we can include in our security and ops review. Specifically we need:

- Detailed staging and prod rollout timeline (milestones + handoff points)
- Integration steps for API auth, data flows, and telemetry hooks
- Canary scope (volume slices, customer cohorts, rollback criteria)
- Evidence of encryption at rest/in transit and KMS options
- Runbook excerpt for a failed canary (SLOs, alerting, fallback)

Would you be able to submit a short Q&A doc and a canary inventory CSV by end of next week (23rd)? Procurement copied here will need the doc for our internal RFP packet.

ZenithShore Financial

Emma — thanks for the clear list. We can deliver a concise Q&A plus the inventory CSV and a short runbook excerpt. High-level plan below; I'll circulate the draft artifacts for review by EOW next Thursday (23rd).

High-level delivery plan
- 11/18: Internal run-through with integration engineers (Jonas) + security (Neha)
- 11/23: Draft Q&A PDF + canary_inventory.csv + runbook excerpt -> sent to Emma & procurement
- 11/24-11/25: Address clarifications from your team
- 11/27: Finalized doc package and signoff link to DocuSign for the SOW addendum

Quick answers to the items you listed:
- Staging->Prod timeline: typical 2-week staging, 3-day canaries, 1-week monitoring window before full cutover (details in draft)
- Auth/data flows: OAuth2 mTLS option for private deployments; token scoping for hosted API. Will include sequence diagrams.
- Canary scope: we typically start with 1% traffic or 5k requests/day (whichever is smaller), escalate to 5% after 72 hours if error budget OK.
- KMS: We support customer-managed KMS for Private (AWS KMS/HSM) and our hosted service uses envelope encryption with per-tenant keys.
- Runbook: we'll provide SLO thresholds, alert triggers, and automated rollback triggers for model fallback.

I'll attach draft v0.2 of the Q&A for initial review.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: zenithshore_rfi_implementation_answers_v0.2.pdf

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:36:00 -0800
Subject: Canary inventory + proposed staging timeline (draft)

Emma / Kimberly — attaching the canary inventory CSV and a short runbook stub. Highlights below: please treat this as a technical draft for your ops/security review.

Canary inventory highlights (see attached 'canary_inventory.csv'):
- Canary cohorts: internal-test (0.1%), pilot-customers (1%), geo-slice (US-west 0.5%)
- Traffic profile: token length distribution, average latency targets, retry budget
- Data scope: no customer PII persisted; request traces truncated to 256 chars for debugging

Staging timeline (detailed in draft)
- Day 0-3: infra provisioning + contract network peering (if Private/VPC)
- Day 4-10: smoke tests + integration tests using synthetic traffic and selected pilot accounts
- Day 11-13: canary period step 1 (pilot-customers 1%)
- Day 14-17: observe, verify telemetry, escalate to step 2 (geo-slice)
- Day 18: if stable, coordinated cutover window for broader ramp

Rollback and escalation
- Immediate rollback if error rate > 2x baseline or if high-severity alerts fired (pager escalations to on-call SRE).
- Automated model fallback to smaller model variant when latency SLOs violated.

Notes on evidence for procurement/security
- We will include KMS key policy examples, TLS endpoint cert chain details, and a SOC2 summary extract in the final package.

Attachment: canary_inventory.csv, runbook-canary-stub.md

Kimberly/Team — procurement is comfortable with the high-level timeline but asked for two clarifications before we include this in the RFP packet:

1) Telemetry taxonomy: please provide exact metric names & units for error_rate, latency_p50/p95/p99, token_throughput, and kv_cache_hit_ratio so we can map them to our dashboards.
2) Data handling: confirm that request/response bodies are not logged to persistent storage in hosted mode and provide the retention period for traces.

Also, can you publish the package to a shared Drive instead of email? I will route to procurement once that is uploaded.

Thanks,
Emma

Subject: Final: ZenithShore implementation validation package (links + next steps)

Emma / Procurement — thank you for the clarifying questions. We uploaded the final package to your shared Drive and created the DocuSign envelope for the SOW addendum. Summary and links below.

Package summary (final)
- Q&A PDF: zenithshore_rfi_implementation_answers_v1.0.pdf (addresses timeline, auth options, KMS, telemetry, SLOs)
- Canary inventory: canary_inventory.csv (cohorts + traffic slices + rollback criteria)
- Runbook excerpt: runbook-canary-stub.md (SLO thresholds, alert routing, rollback automation)
- Evidence: SOC2 extract + KMS key policy example + TLS cert chain snippet

Links:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBzZenithShore-RFI-v2
- DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/some-docusign-link/ZEN-034

Telemetry mapping (exact metric names we will emit)
- redwood.requests.error_rate (percent, unit: %)
- redwood.requests.latency_ms.p50 / p95 / p99 (milliseconds, unit: ms)
- redwood.tokens.throughput (tokens/sec, unit: tokens/s)
- redwood.kv_cache.hit_ratio (ratio 0-1, unit: fraction)

Data handling confirmation
- Hosted API: request/response payloads are not persisted beyond ephemeral tracing. Traces retain up to 30 days by default; request/response bodies truncated to 256 characters and redacted if flagged as sensitive.
- Private/VPC: customer-managed logging options available; retention controlled by customer's logging policy.

Next steps / ask
- Please confirm receipt and approval on the DocuSign link by 11/30 so procurement can close the packet.
- If you want a brief ops-level walkthrough of the runbook and telemetry mapping, Jonas can host a 30-min session next week.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
